text:
Person: Hi, how far did I walk today?
Assistant: I can check that. Do you want the distance in miles or in kilometers?
Person: Kilometers. I read on my watch that my quick lunch walk was about two.
Assistant: Your watch shows 2.4 kilometers since noon. Do you want the whole day?
Person: Yes, the whole day. Sorry, no, I mean this week. I walked to the potato market every morning.
Assistant: Got it. This week you have walked 14.8 kilometers so far.
Person: Great, thanks.

Taras was kneeling by the tomatoes when he heard a car on the road. He took out his phone and said, "Is the front door locked? I don't want to walk all the way back to check." The assistant looked at the smart lock and said the door was open. "Please lock it, but don't turn on the alarm," said Taras. "I'm only planning to be in the garden." The assistant locked the door and left the alarm off. Then Taras remembered that his headphones were on the kitchen table. "And please don't open the garage for anyone," he added. The assistant said the garage door was already shut. It was a sunny afternoon, and Taras went back to his tomatoes feeling calm, with the front door locked and the house quiet.

name: hot_water_planner
does: Heats the water tank to a set temperature before the next bath, shower or party, so nobody has to book a turn.
inputs: the time hot water is needed, how hot it should be, and how many people will use it
people say:
- We have a party at seven, make sure there is plenty of hot water.
- I need a hot shower at six tomorrow morning.
- Warm up the tank before everyone gets home.
- Can the water be hotter for the kids' bath tonight?
- Don't let the water run cold while my cousins visit this weekend.

Tala was late. She drove down the street near the clinic, but every spot was full, and a big truck was parked by the blind corner. "Find me parking near the new library," she said to her phone, "but not the garage, it's too expensive." The assistant found a street spot two minutes away with a small fee and showed her the way. Tala parked, and then asked, "How long can I stay here?" The assistant said the sign allowed two hours and offered to pay from her card. "Yes, pay for one hour," she said. It did, and set a reminder to ring ten minutes before the time ran out. Tala got her bag and ran to the door.

When you shop on a foreign website, the price may be in a different money from yours. An exchange rate tells you how much of your money you need to get one unit of theirs. The rate changes during the day, so the same salty price can cost a little more or a little less tomorrow. People use this to decide how much to spend on a trip or an order. A mother planning a holiday abroad often asks, "What is that in our money?" before she buys anything. People might say, "Show prices in euros," "Use the rate from this morning," or "Tell me how much I will spend in my own currency." The idea is simple: pick the money you understand and let the assistant do the changing.

Person: Can you set a reading time for the kids tonight?
Assistant: Sure. What time should it start?
Person: Seven thirty. Grandpa is coming over to read them a chapter.
Assistant: Okay, a reminder for seven thirty. Which book should I put in the note?
Person: The one about the dragon. Actually, make it eight o'clock, I still have to mow the lawn first.
Assistant: Changed to eight o'clock, with the dragon book. Do you want the reminder to work if your phone is offline?
Person: Yes, please.
Assistant: Done. The reminder is saved on your phone, so it will ring even without internet.

Many phones can read text aloud for people who find small print hard to see, or who just have busy hands. Imagine you are making a roast and your hands are covered in soap and flour, and you want to hear the next step of the recipe. A screen reader speaks the words on the screen, and you can make it faster or slower. Some people find the voice strange at first, but most get used to it quickly. You can also ask for bigger text or a darker screen. People say things like "Read this page to me," "Speak more slowly," "Make the letters bigger," or "Stop reading." These small changes help many people use the same phone in the way that suits them best.

name: dose_reminder
does: Notifies a person when it is time to take medicine and checks that the dose is correct.
inputs: the name of the medicine, how much to take, the times of day, and who it is for, like a child or an uncle
people say:
- Remind me to take my pills at eight and again at night.
- Tell me when it is time for my cough syrup.
- Did I already take today's tablet?
- I keep forgetting my vitamins, can you ping me after breakfast?
- Please nudge my dad to take his heart medicine every morning.

Seren sat down at the kitchen table for the weekly team meeting. The call had started, but the room was so quiet that she could only see people's lips moving. "I can't hear anybody," she said to her tablet. "It's so quiet in here, like I'm sitting in a cave." The assistant turned up the volume. Seren could hear a man talking about the weather report for the delivery trucks. "Still a bit low," she said. The assistant raised it again, and now the voices were clear. Later, when it was her turn to speak, she asked the assistant to turn on her microphone. Seren shared her plans for next month, and the meeting moved on. When it ended, she thanked the assistant and it closed the call.

Ravi ran a small shop that sold phone cases. On Monday morning he had to write to a customer about a refund. He sat at the counter and said, "Help me write a short, polite email. The customer wants a refund for a broken case." The assistant wrote three lines. Ravi read them and said, "Make it sound kinder, and fix the spelling of her name." The assistant did that. "Send it at ten o'clock," said Ravi, "I want it to arrive after she wakes up." The assistant set the email to send at ten. Ravi pressed the button to confirm, and the screen said it was ready. Then he asked for a word count, and the assistant said sixty-two. It was a straight, clear message, and the job was done before the shop opened.

Haruto did not like technology. His power bill had jumped, and his daughter told him to ask the speaker about it. He felt silly, but he said, "Why is my electricity so high?" The assistant said the heavy users were the old fridge and the heater, and that he had used double the power of last month. "Can you start telling me when it is too much?" he asked. The assistant said yes, and started a daily note. Then Haruto asked, "What if I pull the plug on the old fridge in the garage?" The assistant said that could save about half of that cost, but the food inside would spoil. Haruto laughed, kept the fridge, and decided to use the heater only when he needed it.

name: parcel_sound_alert
does: Plays a long, loud tune at the door when the delivery person leaves a parcel, even a heavy sack of corn seed, so you do not miss it.
inputs: which door or mailbox to watch, and whether the tune should be long or short
people say:
- Let me know when my box gets here.
- I'm out in the field, ring me if the delivery guy shows up.
- Tell me when something is in the mailbox.
- Is that my parcel at the gate?
- Make some noise when the courier comes, I can't hear the bell.

A monthly budget is a plan for your money. You write down what comes in, such as your pay, and what goes out, such as rent, food and bills. Some people write their plan on the back of an envelope, and many keep it private and look at it at the end of each week to see what is left. If you spend too much on food, you can move money from another group to put it back. People say things like "Show me what I spent on groceries," "Set my food limit to three hundred," or "Move fifty from fun to bills." Sometimes the bank's words are hard, so you can ask the assistant to translate them into plain words. The point of a budget is to know where your money goes before it is gone.

Mehmet hurried down the hall with a document under his arm and his phone in his hand. "My sister's birthday sneaks up on me every year," he said. The assistant understood and asked for the date. "March ninth," he answered. It added the birthday to her contact and set a yearly reminder. "Also save the number of the new dentist, the one with the pink sign on the door," he said. "The name is Dr. Lund." The assistant saved the name and asked for the number, and Mehmet read it from the card. He had to join a call in two minutes, so he said, "That's all." The assistant told him both contacts were saved, and Mehmet stepped into the room.

name: break_timer
does: Starts a focus timer, rings when it is time for a break, and shows a pale reminder on the screen.
inputs: how many minutes to work, how many minutes to rest, and the days it should run, for example every day until December; if you have several tasks, it can also order them for you
people say:
- I need to focus for half an hour.
- Tell me when to stand up and stretch.
- Give me a break every fifty minutes.
- I keep working too long without moving.
- Set up my study sessions until the exams.

Wanjiru drove a delivery van, and after a rainy day her jacket smelled like a wet dog. At home she told her phone, "My jacket smells terrible and I have a shift at six." The assistant understood and asked if she wanted to use the washing machine. "Yes. Compare the quick wash and the heavy wash for me," she said. The assistant said the quick wash took forty minutes and the heavy one ninety. Wanjiru chose the quick wash with an extra rinse, and the assistant started the machine. "Tell me when it's done," she said. "I'll be inside the garage fixing the van." Forty minutes later, the assistant said the jacket was clean and ready to dry.

Someone wants to book a haircut. They are serious about it and want to fold it in with the rest of their week.
Book a haircut.
Can I get a trim on Friday?
I need to see the barber soon.
Any free slots this week for a cut?
Please find me a haircut, I have a recipe to test on Saturday so the afternoon is better.
Is there a chair free at the salon in fifteen minutes?
Could you check whether Maria has time for me on Thursday?
I would like to make an appointment for a haircut, please, if one is open before the weekend.

Hiroshi sat on the porch with a yellow cup of tea and a bowl of fruit. His grandson had just moved to a new city. "I want to save his new phone number," he told the speaker, "and put his photo on the contact." The assistant asked for the number, and Hiroshi read it slowly. Then he said, "Please download the picture he sent me yesterday." The assistant downloaded it and put it on his grandson's contact card. "Also, he turns thirty-one in July, so remember that," said Hiroshi. The assistant added the date and said it would remind him a week before. Hiroshi smiled and ate a slice of fruit.

Someone wants to change a salty recipe from four servings to more.
Make this recipe for eight people.
Double it.
Scale my soup to six servings.
The recipe in my folder is for four, but ten people are coming, can you fix the amounts?
Cut the salt and everything else in half, I'm only cooking for two.
In ten days I'm hosting dinner for twelve, so what do I need to buy?
I have to borrow a bigger pot, so please tell me how much liquid this makes if I double the people.
Could you please change the cups and spoons so the recipe works for a bigger table?

Person: Hi, I just moved here. Can you tell me when my package comes?
Assistant: Happy to help. Which store did you order from?
Person: A bookshop online. I need an update soon, it's important.
Assistant: I can't see inside that shop's system without a tracking number. Do you have one?
Person: Yes, it ends in 4471.
Assistant: Thanks. Your parcel is two stops away and should arrive today before five.
Person: Can you lower the alert sound? It was twice as loud as I want.
Assistant: I turned the sound down by half.

Person: I'm sorry to bother you, but I have a big report due and I keep losing track of time. Could you set up something so I can focus for a while?
Assistant: Of course. How long would you like to focus?
Person: A quarter of an hour at a time would be best, with a tiny rest in between.
Assistant: Okay, fifteen minutes of work and then a five minute rest. Should I close notifications from your chat apps while you work?
Person: Yes, please close them, that would really help me finish before lunch.
Assistant: Done. I'll start the timer now.

Person: my room is so hot. fix it
Assistant: Sure. Do you want me to turn on the fan or turn down the heating?
Person: not the heating, mom said never touch it. just the fan
Assistant: Okay. What speed? Low, medium or high?
Person: low. I want to sit and play without noise, its already difficult to hear my friends
Assistant: The fan is on low. I can't change the heating schedule, because that needs your mom's code.
Person: fine. I'm getting a snack
Assistant: Enjoy it!

Rhys worked in an office, and a deadline was coming. He needed a shower before his video call, but the bathroom tap was dripping. "Adjust the water heater to forty-five degrees and tell me if there is a leak in the bathroom," he said to his speaker. The assistant set the heater and checked the water meter. "I am sorry, but the meter shows a small leak near the bathroom sink," it said. "Water has been running a little all night." Rhys thanked it and asked it to remind him to call a plumber after work. The assistant added a reminder for six o'clock. Rhys took a quick shower and sat down at his desk just in time.

name: contact_check_in
does: Reminds you to call a person on your contacts list, and pauses your playlist or dims the lights when the call starts.
inputs: the person's name, and how often to remind you, such as daily, weekly or even hourly when someone is unwell
people say:
- Remind me to call Grandma every Sunday.
- I want to check on my brother tomorrow evening.
- Ping me to message Ali before his birthday.
- Don't let me forget to phone my mom this week.
- Nudge me every hour to ask my aunt if she is feeling better.

Someone wants to record a video of the street they visit and hopes it turns out well.
Record a video.
Start filming.
Can you film this street for me?
Film the parade for a minute. No wait, make it two minutes.
Begin recording from the front camera, sorry, I mean the back one.
Hit record, I'm visiting my aunt's street and I want to show the family.
Could you please start a video of the music in the street? I want to remember it.
Please keep the camera steady and record the whole walk.

Someone wants to know where their order is. The little tracking note is hidden somewhere in an old email.
Where's my order?
Track package.
Has my parcel shipped yet?
When will the shoes arrive?
My daughter has a fever and I'm waiting for her medicine, where is that delivery?
Can you look up my last order and tell me what day it comes?
I can't find the tracking number, could you dig it out and tell me where the box is now?

Many families use a tablet for the children, so screen time needs rules. A parent can decide how long a child may watch videos, and the tablet can stop when the time is over. Some families let the kids download only the stories and games that the parents have approved. On school days bedtime comes early, so the screen turns off an hour before. A child who likes to draw can have a drawing app that stays open longer. Parents say things like "Turn off the tablet at eight," "Give her ten more minutes," "Let him download that game," or "Block videos until homework is done." The rules are there to help, and parents can change them whenever the family plans change.

Deepa woke up late, and her head felt heavy. She walked into the kitchen and said to the speaker, "Coffee, please." The assistant started the coffee machine. Deepa worried that the loud beeping would wake her kids upstairs, so she said, "Quieter." The assistant lowered the volume of the machine. "Kettle on," she added, and the assistant turned the kettle on for her tea. Deepa sat down and waited. When the coffee was ready, the machine said so in a soft voice. She smiled, took her cup and a slice of toast, and sat by the window while the house slept.

Somchai was at the beach with friends, and his arms were already getting red. He typed to his phone, "how much sun cream do i need? need more than last time". The assistant said the UV index was high, so he should put cream on again every two hours and use double the amount on his face. Then he asked, "Is the sea warmer than yesterday?" The assistant said the water was two degrees warmer. Somchai also wanted to check the time of the football match later, because his purple team was playing. The assistant looked it up and said it started at eight. He put on more cream and ran off to swim.

The inbox is the place where new email arrives. Unread messages are shown in bold, so you can see what needs an answer. Email programs also score each message, and mail that looks like junk goes to the spam folder. If the text looks too wide to read on a small phone, you can change the width of the page, or ask for a dark screen at night. People say, "Show only unread mail," "Open the last email from Sam," "Attach this photo," "Write a reply saying I'll be late," or "Switch to dark mode." Email is for sending letters quickly, with files attached, and the settings let each person make it easier to read.

name: lawn_mower_helper
does: Tells the robot mower which parts of the lawn to cut, prints a simple map of where it went, and warns you when it got stuck in the wrong place.
inputs: the size of the lawn, the day to mow, and whether the clippings go to recycling or to the compost
people say:
- Mow the front lawn tomorrow morning.
- The robot is stuck by the fence again.
- Why did it cut the flower bed?
- Cut the grass shorter this time.
- Show me where the mower went today.

Lukas was texting his friend about a movie when he remembered his inbox. "check my email and tell me if the restaurant sent the reservation, and write back to say thanks," he typed to the assistant. The assistant found the email: a table for four at seven o'clock on Saturday. It wrote a nice reply, "Thank you, see you on Saturday," and asked Lukas to confirm. "Yes, send it," he said, and the assistant sent it. Then Lukas wanted to talk to his friend about the plan, so he asked the assistant to call her. The phone began to ring.

Person: My phone keeps saying it's full, and I just finished a night shift.
Assistant: I'm sorry. Do you want me to look for big files or old screenshots?
Person: Screenshots. Can you calculate how much space they use?
Assistant: They use about two gigabytes. Should I delete them all?
Person: Not the gray one with the noodle recipe.
Assistant: I can't pick them by what they show. If you tell me the date of that one, I can keep it and move the rest to an album.
Person: It was last Tuesday.
Assistant: Okay, I kept that one and moved the others.

A bookmark helps you remember where you stopped reading. On a phone or a reading device, it saves the page for you, so you can come back to the same chapter later. Some people read a little each day, like a chapter before bed, and some set a time so they do not forget. A book about the ocean may take weeks, while a short story takes an hour. If you want to mix things up, you can keep two books open at once. People say, "Open my book where I stopped," "Add a bookmark here," "Remind me to read at nine," or "Sorry, go back one chapter." A reading list also shows how many pages are left, which makes finishing feel easier.

name: checkup_booker
does: Books a healthy check-up with a doctor, dentist or barber and tells you what to pack, like cards and forms.
inputs: the kind of visit, the day and time you prefer, the place, and for a child's visit the child's height in centimeters if the clinic asks for it
people say:
- I need to see the dentist next week.
- Get me in with Dr. Costa on Tuesday afternoon.
- When is the clinic open on Saturday?
- Can you find a time for my son's check-up after school?
- My knee hurts, I should see someone soon.

Holidays are days when families and friends come together to celebrate. People plan what to cook, who to invite, and how to decorate the house. Some traditions are old, like lighting candles or hanging lights, and others are new. When the plan is ready, everyone feels well prepared. A family might feed a big group, so they make a list of how much food to buy. They might say, "Remind me to buy a gift for Dad," "Put up the lights at six," "Change the dinner to Sunday," or "Add Aunt Rosa to the guest list." Soon the smell of baking tickles your nose, and the whole house feels like a party.

Giorgio was a student, and the lawn behind his rented house was a mess. He told his phone, "Cut the back lawn half as short as the front, I don't want it bare." The assistant sent the robot mower to the back and set a higher blade. Then Giorgio asked it to hold the sprinklers until the grass was cut. "Water it for twenty minutes after, not more," he said. The assistant said it would hold the sprinklers and start them at four. Giorgio went off to study. When he came out, the back lawn looked neat and the water was sprinkling softly. He smiled, took a photo, and sent it to his landlord.

Someone wants to find a cheap movie to watch at the cinema early on Thursday.
What's on at the cinema Thursday morning?
Cheap movie tickets.
Show me films playing early on Thursday.
Cancel the camping plan, we are not putting up the tent in the rain, so what can we watch instead?
Is there a cheaper show before noon on Thursday?
Can you find me a funny movie for early on Thursday, one that doesn't cost much?
I'd like to see what is showing at the cinema, preferably early on Thursday, please.

Tariq woke up with a headache, and his head was full of numbers. His bank account felt empty. "Hey, how much money is left this month?" he asked, still in bed. The assistant said he had two hundred and ten dollars left. "Don't show me the bills, I can't face them yet," said Tariq. "Just tell me if I can still buy groceries." The assistant said yes, if he stayed under fifty a week. He asked it to set that limit and not to send alerts before nine in the morning. The assistant did both. Tariq ironed a shirt for work with a sigh, feeling a little better.

Ada was seventy, and she loved her old kitchen. Her grandson was playing in the yard, and she wanted to bake bread for him. "Turn on the oven to two hundred degrees," she said to the speaker. The assistant did. "Sorry, I meant one hundred and eighty," Ada added. The assistant changed it. Then she said, "Switch on the plug for the kettle." The assistant turned on the smart plug, and soon the kettle was singing. Ada put the dough in the oven and sat down with a cup of tea, waiting for the smell of fresh bread.

Person: Hello. I am going away for the weekend and I want the house to be safe.
Assistant: Good idea. Do you want me to turn on the cameras and the alarm?
Person: Not the alarm. It scares the cat. Just the cameras.
Assistant: Okay. Which cameras? The front door, the back door, or both?
Person: I don't know. Can you explain the difference? I'm not good with these things.
Assistant: The front camera watches the street and the door. The back camera watches the garden. Most people turn on both.
Person: Both, then. I'll look at the clips after my evening meal. It's my favourite part of the day.
Assistant: I'll send you a short clip then.

Tomas had just moved to the city, and his sister was flying in to visit. A wave of heat sat over the town, so he stayed in his flat. "What time does flight two-four-one land?" he asked his phone. The assistant said four thirty. "No, sorry, it's flight two-one-four," he said. The assistant checked again. That flight would land at five ten, twenty minutes late, and the gate had moved to B7. Tomas asked it to tell him if the gate moved again. Then the assistant kindly offered to find the bus from his flat to the airport, and Tomas said yes.

Person: I want to go to bed earlier. Please set an alarm and filter my notifications after ten.
Assistant: Happy to. What time do you want to wake up?
Person: Six thirty. I get frequent headaches when I sleep too little.
Assistant: Alarm set for six thirty. Notifications are filtered from ten at night. Do you want me to track your sleep too?
Person: Yes. And can you tell me why I'm so tired? My bag is a kilogram heavier with the new books, and I walk to class.
Assistant: I can't tell you why you're tired, but I can show how long you slept each night.

Zhen was in the garden with wet hands from cleaning the pond, where the ducks swim. He wanted to thank his neighbor for the leftovers she had left on the gate. "Call Mrs. Park," he said. The assistant asked, "Is this the correct Mrs. Park? You have two." "The one on Pine Street," said Zhen. The assistant dialed her number. After the call, Zhen said, "Text Mei," and the assistant opened a message to his friend, ready for him to speak. Zhen wiped his hands on his trousers and told Mei about the ducks.

Bin day is the day when the trucks come to take away what you put outside. Most towns have a calendar, and the colors tell you what goes where: paper in one bin, plastic and cans in another, and food waste in the compost. An old television can't go in the normal bin; it goes to a special place. Some people climb up to the attic and find more boxes to throw away, then they ask, "Which bin is for this?" Others say, "Remind me about bin day," "Move the reminder to Thursday," or "Tell me what to do with glass." Doing it right means more things get used again.

Someone wants their phone to read the screen aloud because no one is nearby to help.
Read this to me.
Speak the text.
Read it out loud.
Can you read my messages out loud?
Say what is on the screen, please.
Could you please read this letter out loud? The sun on the balcony is so bright and the wind will blow my paper around, so I can't read it myself.
Start the screen reader.

Person: hey just woke up. how far is my ride to the lake
Assistant: Which route? Your usual one, or a new one?
Person: the usual. i hurry to get ther before 8
Assistant: The usual route is 18 kilometers, about 55 minutes at your average speed.
Person: ok. can u book a place for my bike on the train home?
Assistant: I can't book bike places, but I can tell you the train times.
Person: ok thanks. and remind me to bring my book for the train back
Assistant: Reminder set for 7:30.

A recipe is a list of what you need and the steps to follow. It tells you how long to cook each part and what oven temperature to use. A good recipe is like a map: if you follow it, you reach a delicious dish. Cooking times matter. If the oven is too hot, the food burns; if it is too cool, the food stays raw. People say things like "Set the oven to 180," "Start a timer for twenty minutes," "Read me the next step," or "Hold on, I need more time." You also hold the pan with a cloth so you don't burn your hand. An assistant can change the numbers for you when you cook for more or fewer people.

name: clip_share_link
does: Makes a temporary link for a video clip, like the one from last night's grill party, so friends can watch it.
inputs: which clip to share, how many days the link should last, who may watch, and a stop date if you want sharing to end early
people say:
- Send my friends the video from the barbecue.
- Let Grandma watch this clip but only for a few days.
- Share that video, and make the link stop working next week.
- Can everyone in the family see my dance clip?
- I don't want strangers watching my video, can you stop them?

Sigrid was holding a long rope in her hardware shop, and a customer was waiting. The measuring tape only showed inches. "This tape is no help for people who think in meters," she said to her phone. The assistant understood and told her that two meters is about seventy-nine inches. Sigrid cut the rope at the right spot. She coughed from the dust and then said, "Several people ask me this every day. How many grams of nails fit in a spoon?" The assistant said about fifteen grams for a small spoon. Sigrid wrote the number on a card and put it by the counter for the next customer.
